Marissa —

Thanks for the note and the materials. Quick answers from procurement/legal POV:
- Procurement lead (procurement@praxishealth.com) needs ~10 business days to review order form language once the commercial terms are stable.
- Legal can do a preliminary review of a draft MSA/DPA in ~7 business days; final redlines depend on whether we need to escalate to privacy counsel for the DPA.
- We will need SOC 2 Type II (most recent) and a brief data flow diagram. Pen test report: desirable but not mandatory for the pilot.

Proposed tweak: move the signature target earlier by a week if Redwood can provide the SOC 2 evidence and the final acceptance criteria within 5 business days after pilot completion. That gives us room to land PO approval within your proposed window.

I’ll attach our standard PO template so your team can confirm any commercial fields that need to be filled out.

—Ellen

Hi all —

Adding the technical acceptance lane and a suggested test plan so engineering can sign off quickly:
- Pilot specifics: 3 business days, 2 customer integration endpoints (staging + canary), sample dataset limited to non-PHI fields.
- Metrics to capture: token throughput, 95th/99th latency, error rate by route, and per-request provenance header requirement.
- Rollback criteria: any data residency violation or sustained error rate > 2% over 30m window.

On the order form sequencing: recommend the following flow to avoid parallel redline churn:
1) Technical acceptance complete -> group signs off (engineering + security)
2) Commercial terms locked in the order form (pricing + billing cadence)
3) Legal receives agreed order form + MSA/DPA bundle for single consolidated review

I’ll be available for a short technical walkthrough with Praxis engineers mid-week if helpful.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions Architecture — Redwood Inference

Also, we can accelerate signature by one week as long as the SOC 2 package arrives within 3 business days after pilot completion and the consolidated redlines come back on schedule. I’ve attached the PO template — procurement will fill commercial fields once the order form is final.
